literal: Than performing a thousand sacrifices by pouring offerings, not eating [flesh] by destroying the life of a single being is better.
translation: Abstaining from killing even a single living being and eating its flesh is far better than performing a thousand sacrifices by pouring rich offerings into the fire.
modern: அவிப்பொருள்களைச் சொரிந்து ஆயிரம் வேள்விகளைச் செய்வதை விட, ஓர் உயிரைக் கொன்று அதன் உடலை உண்ணாமல் இருப்பது மிகவும் நல்லது.
explanation: This couplet compares ritual piety with ethical compassion. The author states that performing a thousand elaborate fire sacrifices (வேட்டல்) with rich offerings (அவி) is of lesser value than the simple act of refraining from killing a single living being (உயிர் செகுத்து) and eating its flesh (உண்ணாமை). The word 'அவி' refers to the sacred offerings like ghee or grains poured into the sacrificial fire, while 'செகுத்து' means destroying or killing. By placing the preservation of a single life above a thousand grand religious rituals, the couplet emphasizes that non-killing and compassion are the highest virtues.
